subsystems.name: Cryogenic tanks
subsystems.role: hold liquid oxygen, methane or hydrogen at tens of kelvin for months without venting the propellant away.

subsystems.name: Thermal control
subsystems.role: fight the ~300 K environment around the tanks.

subsystems.name: Fluid management in microgravity
subsystems.role: make liquid behave without gravity, so it sits over the outlet and can be measured.
parts: propellant management devices or liquid acquisition screens

subsystems.name: Transfer interface
subsystems.role: connects depot to tanker and to the customer vehicle.

subsystems.name: Avionics and station-keeping
subsystems.role: holds the depot in a stable orbit and runs the transfer autonomously.

subsystems.name: Resupply logistics
subsystems.role: the tankers and ground operations that keep the depot filled.

buildSteps.title: Design the tank and thermal shield
buildSteps.detail: Engineers size tank volume against the boil-off budget over the mission life, trading extra insulation and cryocooler power against launch mass.

buildSteps.title: Fabricate the tank
buildSteps.detail: Shells are spun or welded from lightweight alloy or wound composite, then proof-tested and cleaned for oxygen service.

buildSteps.title: Fit internal fluid management
buildSteps.detail: Propellant management devices, baffles and gauging sensors are installed inside the tank before closure.

buildSteps.title: Apply insulation
buildSteps.detail: Multilayer insulation blankets and, where needed, sprayed foam and vapour-cooled shields are wrapped around the tank.

buildSteps.title: Integrate cryocoolers and plumbing
buildSteps.detail: Cold heads, reliquefaction lines, fill and drain couplings and vent valves are attached and leak-checked.

buildSteps.title: Launch
buildSteps.detail: The depot flies to orbit as a payload, typically empty or lightly loaded, inside a launcher fairing or as part of a stage.

buildSteps.title: Check out on orbit
buildSteps.detail: Solar arrays and the sunshade deploy, the cryocooler is commissioned and the depot holds station while awaiting a tanker.

buildSteps.title: Transfer propellant
buildSteps.detail: A tanker docks, lines are chilled down to prevent flashing, a small thrust settles the liquid over the outlet, and fluid is pumped or pressure-transferred across.

buildSteps.title: Serve a customer
buildSteps.detail: A departing spacecraft docks, takes on propellant and departs; the depot is topped up by later tanker flights.

prerequisites.why: filling a depot takes many tanker flights, so cheap reflight is what makes the economics work.
depots must be met repeatedly without a crew aboard.
settling liquid, gauging mass and transferring without loss has only been shown at small scale.
zero-boil-off storage needs coolers that run for years at tens of watts of lift.
without agreed couplings and protocols, each spacecraft needs a bespoke depot.

pathway.unlocks: confidence that docking, chilling and transferring liquids works in microgravity.

pathway.milestone: large-scale cryogenic transfer between two spacecraft
pathway.unlocks: the basis for the Artemis lunar-lander architecture, which needs orbital refuelling.

pathway.milestone: a persistently stored depot in low Earth orbit
pathway.unlocks: routine departure of loaded spacecraft to higher orbits and the Moon.

pathway.milestone: depots at cislunar or Lagrange points
pathway.unlocks: reusable deep-space tugs and lower cost per kilogram to Mars and beyond.
